history.summary: Soreng Thakurbari is a HINDU temple in Soreng town, Soreng district, West Sikkim - officially listed by the Sikkim Ecclesiastical Affairs Department in its district-wise list of Hindu mandirs ('Soreng Thakurbari, Soreng, Soreng'). Tripadvisor lists it as the top thing to do in Soreng; a directory listing rates it 4.0/5 (3 reviews), one review noting 'Hare Krishna', suggesting a Vaishnavite Krishna shrine. No published founding history could be located - dynasty and period are undocumented (verify locally). IMPORTANT NON-CONFLATION NOTE: seq 925 (id thakurbari-temple-gangtok) documents the famous Shri Thakurbari Temple on M.G. Marg, Gangtok (built 1935) - that is a DIFFERENT temple from this Soreng one, so this row gets its own id and entry. 'Thakurbari' is a common Bengali-derived name meaning 'God's home' (Thakur = God, Bari = home), used by several distinct shrines across Sikkim, West Bengal, Bihar and Bangladesh. MEDIA NOTE: image searches for this temple returned only photos of the Gangtok Thakurbari (a different, grander complex); no reliable Soreng-specific image was found, so media is left empty.

name: Soreng Thakurbari
town_description: Soreng is a small town in the Soreng district of West Sikkim (the district was carved out of West Sikkim in December 2021), at ~1,700 m in the Himalayan foothills. It is the district headquarters and a quiet local market town; tourism infrastructure is thin compared to nearby Pelling and Jorethang. The Thakurbari is the town's best-known religious site per Tripadvisor.
tradition: Hinduism (Vaishnavite leanings per visitor review; deity unconfirmed - verify)

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Bagdogra (IXB), approx. 130-150 km (verify); Pakyong Airport is closer but has limited flights.
travel.railway: Nearest major railway station is New Jalpaiguri (NJP); note one directory site claims 'Darjeeling railway station 10 km' which is implausible and not repeated here (verify).
travel.road: In Soreng town; reachable by taxi/shared jeep from Jorethang, Gyalshing (Geyzing) and Pelling.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for clear mountain weather (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published (verify locally); small-town Hindu temples in Sikkim typically open early morning and evening.
